anti_overlap: Does not evaluate whether tonal-theme is the right taxonomy axis in the abstract, or whether five is a well-calibrated count for literacy cadence — that is fd-taxonomy-legibility-design's remit.

Does not evaluate the composition arithmetic between wing bias, kill-share heredity, and playstyle signals, or the hard-gate-vs-soft-bias question for decision 9 — that is fd-loot-bias-composition's remit.
Does not review PixiJS rendering, persistence schema design, or Beat 2 zone/mood mechanics — those are downstream implementation concerns outside the wing-set v0 design's scope.
decision_lens: If a second engineer picked up only the current data model (the 352-entry `Encryptid` type, `RunReportSource`, and `EncryptidMatcher`) months from now and tried to wire in the loot-farming-literacy consumer promised by §11.6, would the wing taxonomy chosen for hatch-mapping today still fit that job unmodified, or would it need a second, incompatible shape bolted on?
focus: Whether the wing taxonomy can actually carry two downstream jobs — hatch-mapping now and loot-farming literacy later (§11.6) — evaluated against the real shape of the current Encryptid/RunReport/matcher data contracts and the 'rooms never change, fauna changes' canon principle for Borgesroom-adjacent systems.
name: fd-dataflow-dual-consumer
persona: Apply the perspective of a data-architecture / live-service content-taxonomy specialist experienced in classification systems that must serve multiple independent downstream consumers over time (an item-tag system reused across crafting, vendor recipes, and league mechanics; a content-rating taxonomy reused across search, recommendation, and moderation) — someone whose first move is always to trace a proposed taxonomy through each consumer's actual data contract end-to-end rather than trust that a single shared vocabulary will serve every future use 'for free.'
review_areas: Data-contract gap check: `types/encryptids/EncryptidTypes.ts`'s `Encryptid` interface (id, name, descriptions, 28-axis `dimensions`, `confidenceRatings`, `justifications`) has no family/wing field today, and `EncryptidMatcher` never references jawnomicon family membership anywhere in its scoring — does the brainstorm's import pipeline (decision 3) actually specify how per-creature family-slug membership gets attached during import, or is 'wing → family pool' assuming a linkage that doesn't exist yet in the target data model?

Two-consumer taxonomy divergence: hatch-mapping needs a taxonomy that biases *acquisition* (which creature you get at extraction), while §11.6's loot-farming literacy needs a taxonomy that biases *drop targeting* inside a room/wing you're already in (per its own text: 'funerary wings lean funerary records' — a room-content bias, not a creature-acquisition bias) — audit whether the five tonal wings, sized and grouped for acquisition-legibility, would still be a sensible unit for loot-table biasing, or whether loot-farming literacy actually wants a finer-grained or differently-axed vocabulary (e.g. per-record-type, per-encounter) the wing set doesn't provide.

Canon-consistency check against §12.3: the shipped Eidolon-influence design states explicitly 'the rooms never change, the fauna changes' as the Borgesian-horror principle for this family of systems — check whether mapping each wing directly onto a fixed family-pool (decision 9) makes a wing's 'fauna' effectively static per roll (the wing determines one fixed pool rather than a varying one), and flag whether that reads as a departure from the room/fauna distinction the delve side has already ruled on for the sibling Eidolon-influence system.

Run-signature data availability: `RunReportSource` exposes `roster` (presence kind/tint/mods/kills across five fixed archetypes — `private`/`evangelist`/`gatekeeper`/`postIronic`/`aspirant`), `waveReached`, `runKills`, `elapsedTime`, `echoShards`, `dropsCollected`, but no enemy-species/family kill breakdown and no pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle fields — check whether decision 2's 'enemy mix → temperament' and open question 2's playstyle-axis mapping are grounded in data the delve sim actually emits today, or whether they require new instrumentation not scoped anywhere in the brainstorm.

Roster-expansion sequencing: decision 3 expands the roster from 352 snapshot entries to the full 645-creature jawnomicon bestiary; verify the wing-set v0 design accounts for the fact that only 546 of those 645 jawnomicon creatures belong to a named family at all (99 are outliers per the families export's own `creatures_in_named_families` count), and that the import pipeline's eidogen-verbatim discipline (no hand-authoring or backfilling) is stated to extend to family membership, not just dimension scores.

Migration/versioning risk: jawnomicon families are versioned (`v16`, built from a `carryFamilyNames.ts` carry-forward/naming pipeline that implies churn across versions) — check whether the wing-set design pins wing definitions to family slugs (stable identifiers, e.g. `death-criers`) or family display names (subject to relabeling, e.g. 'The Death-Criers'), since a wing definition hardcoding display names risks silently drifting from the source-of-truth export on the next jawnomicon families revision.

severity_examples.condition: the import pipeline spec (decision 3 or its implementation plan) doesn't name families.json / family slugs as the verbatim source for wing-pool membership.
severity_examples.scenario: Decision 3's import pipeline is built to bring in eidogen dimensions verbatim per the dual-rater discipline, but no equivalent verbatim-import contract is specified for family/wing membership — if wing membership ends up hand-assigned per creature during import rather than pulled directly from the jawnomicon families export, it silently violates the same dual-rater/no-hand-authoring discipline decision 3 explicitly claims to uphold, corrupting the design's own stated data-integrity bar for the full 645-creature roster.

severity_examples.condition: no explicit check is shown anywhere that the five tonal wings would still make sense as loot-table-biasing units, only that they make sense as hatch-family-pool units.
severity_examples.scenario: The wing taxonomy is locked in Beat 1, sized and grouped for hatch-acquisition legibility (five broad tonal buckets), and §11.6's loot-farming literacy is assumed to bolt on later using those same five buckets — but §11.6's own example ('funerary wings lean funerary records') describes a finer-grained per-record-type bias than 'tonal theme,' so the taxonomy chosen now may need to be re-cut when the loot-literacy consumer actually arrives, undercutting decision 10's framing of the wing stand-in as forward-compatible with 'the full borgesrooms system... next.'

severity_examples.condition: the wing-to-family mapping is specified by display name rather than slug anywhere in the design or its eventual implementation.
severity_examples.scenario: The wing-set design maps wings to jawnomicon families without noting that families are a versioned export (`v16`) with a carry-forward/renaming pipeline — if the wing definitions pin to family display names ('Death-Criers') rather than stable slugs (`death-criers`), a future jawnomicon families revision that renames or re-clusters a family would silently desync the wing pool from its intended member set with no build-time signal.

success_hints: Traces the taxonomy through both consumers' actual mechanics (hatch-matching's per-creature scoring vs. §11.6's per-room drop-table targeting) rather than asserting compatibility or incompatibility without checking each consumer's real shape.

Checks the current `Encryptid` type, `RunReportSource`, and `EncryptidMatcher` against what the brainstorm's decisions assume is already wired, and names the specific gap (no family field, no enemy-mix breakdown, no playstyle axes) rather than a general 'the data model may need work.'

Distinguishes a genuine two-consumer taxonomy conflict from a sequencing non-issue that's legitimately fine to re-cut later per decision 10's explicit 'wing stand-in now, full system next' framing — not every difference between the two consumers' needs is a defect in the v0 design.
Flags the slug-vs-display-name versioning risk concretely, citing the manifest's own versioning/carry-forward machinery rather than a generic 'data may drift' caution.
Recommends a specific taxonomy shape (or confirms the current one is fine) that would serve both consumers, rather than only diagnosing the tension and stopping there.
task_context:
Ideate and evaluate alternatives for the Borgesroom wing-set v0 in After Them — the themed wing identity each delve run rolls, which biases the encryptid matcher's family pools and makes run→creature hatching legible ('this run became this creature'). The current straw proposal is five tonal wings mapped to jawnomicon families: Funerary (Death-Criers/Underworld Court/Night-Comers), Tempest (Tempest-Bringers/Rain-Serpents/Rain-Holders/Maelstrom-Makers), Hearth (Hearth-Bound/Kindly Watchers/Blessing-Bearers/First Teachers), Hungers (Lurking Hunters/Hungers That Think/Monstrous Broods/Wings of Ill Omen), Mirrors (Tricksters/Shape-Thieves/Never-Caught). Evaluate and propose better alternatives on four questions: (1) Is wing-as-tonal-theme the right taxonomy axis at all? Consider alternatives: wings by record type (canon §11.6: 'funerary wings lean funerary records' — wings are archive sections of a Borgesian library), by eidogen dimension cluster, by media-feature region (entropy/rhythm/emotionalTone), by enemy ecology, by player-verb affordance. (2) Is five the right count for Beat 1, given each wing must be felt often enough to build literacy? (3) How should wing bias compose with the other hatch signals (roster kill-share heredity, pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle axes) so hatches stay legible but not deterministic — and never hard-gate the 645-creature roster? (4) The wings will serve TWO consumers — hatch mapping now, loot-farming literacy later (§11.6) — do the two jobs pull toward different taxonomies, and if so which taxonomy serves both? Ground in the actual sources, do not trust summaries: docs/research/2026-08-09-meta-home-loop-teardowns.md, game-design-docs/teardown-arpg-modifiers.md §11-12, game-design-docs/after-them-delve-formation.md (R1-R8), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/families.json (44 families with member lists), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/data/families-prose.yaml (family blurbs), src/sim/habitat/types.ts (MediaFeatures), src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts (scoring), src/ui/RunReport.ts (available run facts).

Grounding for this lens: read `/Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/manifest.json` for the export's own versioning/provenance fields (`artifact_version`, `communities_params`, `naming_batch`, `counts.creatures_in_named_families`) before asserting anything about stability or coverage. Read `types/encryptids/EncryptidTypes.ts` and `src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts` in full to confirm there is currently no family/wing field or reference anywhere in the matcher's data model. Read `src/ui/RunReport.ts`'s exported interfaces for the literal run-fact contract available to the hatch-mapping consumer today. Read `game-design-docs/teardown-arpg-modifiers.md` §11.6 and §12.3 closely — both are short but load-bearing for the two-consumer question.
